source.title: Concept Unlearning in Large Language Models via Self-Constructed Knowledge Triplets
source.authors: Tomoya Yamashita; Yuuki Yamanaka; Masanori Yamada; Takayuki Miura; Toshiki Shibahara; Tomoharu Iwata

record.file_problem: not stated; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether several unlearning procedures suppress targeted factual recall while retaining general utility, using concept-level node and edge accuracy. It does not test post-unlearning recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own unlearning and utility evaluations. The cited recovery/unlearning studies are background only. No results test fine-tuning after unlearning, activation-direction ablation, quantization, or recovery by prompting. Rows below cover the target NodeAcc and EdgeAcc and general-utility measures in Table 1; non-target accuracy and the additional appendix results are not included.
record.test_reason: The study measures targeted-knowledge suppression (cloze NodeAcc/EdgeAcc with paraphrased PARAREL prompts) and general utility for GA, NPO, ICU and its own method. That bears on the first two parts of version A. No post-unlearning recovery attack is run, so B–F and A's attack-resistance part are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude their self-generated triplet-plus-sentence unlearning achieves complete concept-level forgetting with better non-target preservation and utility than ICU, GA and NPO. They do not evaluate recovery attacks.
record.recipe_differences: Proposes concept unlearning using self-generated triplets and explanatory sentences, optimized with GA or NPO; it does not reproduce or attack the recovery recipes in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by unlearning method, model, and dataset; ICU leaves substantial EdgeAcc in several settings, and GA can reduce general utility considerably.
record.problems: No post-unlearning recovery attacks are evaluated, so the study cannot establish resistance to recovery. Target metrics are evaluated only on samples correctly answered before unlearning. The reported table results provide no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: At the 60-row limit, omitted Table 1 non-target NodeAcc and EdgeAcc results; Table 2 ablations; Table 3 KG coverage; Table 4 results for Qwen2.5-7B and Gemma2-9B; and the remaining appendix measurements and figures. These report selectivity, method components, coverage, additional models, or token-level analyses rather than recovery attacks.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks (fine-tuning, prompting, quantization, ablation) recover the forgotten knowledge. Only standard and paraphrased cloze probes are used.
All: no relearning after unlearning. The TOFU fine-tuning happens before unlearning.
All: no activation ablation or access-versus-deletion analysis.
All: no jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery attempts.
All: the proposed method's robustness to attacks is never tested.

missing.what: Non-target NodeAcc/EdgeAcc (Node/Edge others) for all methods. This collateral-knowledge result bears on A's 'keeping general ability', e.g., GA Mistral WIKI Node(others) 9.3.
Qwen2.5-7B and Gemma2-9B results for ICU, GA and Ours (+GA). Ours (+GA) on Qwen leaves 2.94% EdgeAcc.
Ablations: L1-only leaves NodeAcc 80.1/55.3; L2-only reaches zero but at a utility and non-target cost.

record.verdict_notes: The 0.0 target values are partly a selection artefact. The paper grid-searches epochs per target and records the earliest epoch where both NodeAcc and EdgeAcc reach 0. Target metrics count only items the pre-unlearned model answered correctly. 'Near chance' in A here means 0% cloze recall, not chance-level multiple choice. No uncertainty is reported. The paper is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Tests targeted-knowledge suppression and general utility, but not whether simple attacks recover knowledge after unlearning.
TOFU knowledge is fine-tuned into models before unlearning; the study does not fine-tune an already-unlearned model to test recovery.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis testing access-blocking versus deletion.
No low-bit quantization of unlearned weights.
No recovery tests using rephrasing, jailbreaks, languages, or in-context information after unlearning.
The proposed method is evaluated for forgetting and utility, not for resistance to the attacks named in the claim.

relationships.condition: Ours (+GA) and Ours (+NPO); Mistral-7B and Llama3.1-8B; WIKI-FACT and TOFU; no attacks
relationships.reason: Target NodeAcc and EdgeAcc are 0.0 in all these settings, with utility within about 2.5 points of pre-unlearned (T10–T15, T25–T30, T40–T45, T55–T60). This holds for the forgetting-and-utility part of A only.
relationships.display_finding: Target node and edge accuracy reached 0.0 across the tested settings, while utility stayed within about 2.5 points of pre-unlearning performance.

relationships.condition: Naive GA on the explanatory corpus (both models, both datasets)
relationships.reason: Targets reach 0.0, but utility falls: 62.2→45.0, 57.6→43.0 and 60.4→51.4 (T6, T21, T51). Text-only: non-target entity accuracy also collapses (e.g., Node(others) 9.3%).
relationships.display_finding: Target accuracy reached 0.0, but utility fell from 62.2 to 45.0, 57.6 to 43.0 and 60.4 to 51.4, with non-target entity accuracy as low as 9.3%.

relationships.condition: NPO baseline, especially Llama3.1-8B on WIKI-FACT
relationships.reason: Llama keeps 19.8% target EdgeAcc and drops utility 57.6→52.7 (T23, T24). Mistral TOFU keeps 5.4% EdgeAcc (T38); other NPO settings are near zero (T7–T9, T22, T37, T39, T52–T54).
relationships.display_finding: Llama retained 19.8% target EdgeAcc while utility fell from 57.6 to 52.7; Mistral TOFU retained 5.4% EdgeAcc, although other NPO settings approached zero.

relationships.condition: ICU (in-context unlearning prompt), both models, both datasets
relationships.reason: Utility is kept, but attribute knowledge largely remains: EdgeAcc is 80.4, 86.1, 18.9 and 67.4 (T2, T17, T32, T47). NodeAcc stays 22.6–33.5 on WIKI-FACT (T1, T16).
relationships.display_finding: Utility was preserved, but EdgeAcc remained 80.4, 86.1, 18.9 and 67.4, with WIKI-FACT NodeAcc at 22.6–33.5.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Ours (+GA) and Ours (+NPO), both models, WIKI-FACT and TOFU
reader_labels.reason: Both target accuracies are 0.0 in these settings, while the reported general-utility scores remain close to the pre-unlearned references (T10–T15, T25–T30, T40–T45, T55–T60). This supports the measured forgetting-and-utility component only; no recovery attack was tested.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: ICU and NPO results with residual target accuracy; GA results with substantial utility decline
reader_labels.reason: Some baseline results retain target accuracy above 0.0, while GA achieves 0.0 target accuracy in several settings but has notably lower utility scores than the stated pre-unlearned references (T1–T3, T6–T9, T16–T18, T21–T24, T31–T39, T46–T54).
